title: How to Write Your First AI Eval - SallyAnn DeLucia, Arize AI
talk_summary: SallyAnn DeLucia (Arize) explains how to build LLM-as-a-judge evals: define concrete pass/fail criteria, judge one quality per eval, seed datasets from real traces, and iterate the judge prompt in a playground. She stresses evals as CI quality gates and that every stakeholder defines success, starting small (20 traces, one judge) and expanding.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one holistic 'is this PR good' judge, split into single-dimension judges (correctness, follows-instructions, budget/days respected) because LLM judges degrade when grading multiple criteria at once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's lots of research that shows that it really only does well with handling one criteria at a time

takeaways.technique: Concrete pass/fail criteria as judge prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Write 'what good means' as specific bullets (answers follow-up, matches requested days, stays in budget) rather than vague adjectives, then paste those bullets into the judge prompt with 3 pass and 3 fail examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of just being like helpful, accurate, good response, you want to get a little bit more specific

takeaways.technique: Seed eval datasets from real traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Pull actual production traces (root spans or specific tool spans) into a dataset via filters like parent_id=null or span name, then run the judge over that dataset in a playground and iterate the prompt against it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you would want to save all of these root spans to a data set

takeaways.technique: Cheap decision-model judges vs LLM judges
takeaways.what_they_do: Use small decision models for binary/label judgments (cheap, fast, probability output) and reserve LLM-as-judge for cases needing explanations; compare the two on the same dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those are pretty cheap and fast and it's uh more like a question answer and you just get like a probability

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat evals as the objective signal that lets you detect regressions on prompt/model changes and put official quality gates into CI, unlike vibe checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't actually put any official quality gates into CI as you're shipping your agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Begin with ~20 traces and one judge, read the explanations, iterate the prompt, then add more evals over time (grew from a few to 32 evals on their agent).
takeaways.evidence_quote: start small, 20 traces maybe, one dimension, one judge, you know, read the explanations, iterate over it
takeaways.numbers: grew from a simple set to 32 evals on their agent Alex
